title: CDP Tab Identity Design
desc: Tab targeting via targetId+TitleHistory composite key; grap tab field design
steps: DESIGN: CDP tab identity uses composite key. Key='targetId[:8]:currentTitle', Value=CdpTab{TargetId, TitleHistory:List<string>, Domain, LastActive}.

LIFECYCLE: targetId survives tab detach/window-split (renderer moves intact). Invalidated on: page reload, crash recovery, Chrome restart. WebBot restart = full cache eviction OK (no persistence needed).

CACHE: In-process dict keyed by targetId8. Value = CdpTab{TargetId, TitleHistory(LRU cap=8), Domain, LastActive, BrowserPid}. BrowserPid = Chrome browser-process PID for multi-instance filtering (NOT renderer PID -- non-unique across same-site tabs, see step 7). Title stored only inside TitleHistory, never in any dict key.

RECOVERY: On WebBot restart (Chrome alive): Target.getTargets() on each project CDP port -> rebuild cache from live targetId+title+url+browserPid. Covers 'WebBot died, Chrome alive' fully. Historical title variants re-accumulated live. Zero file I/O, no HWND props needed.
SEARCH PRIORITY: 1) targetId prefix match (exact, session-stable) 2) TitleHistory any-entry match (handles dynamic titles: badge counts, play indicators) 3) domain+title fallback (post-restart).

GRAP SYNTAX: tab field in JSON5 -- {proc:'chrome',cdp:PORT,tab:'6B4A2F8C:Gmail'}. Parser: hex8:text -> targetId prefix + title label. title-only -> history search. cdp open returns tab composite string.
WHY NOT rendererPID: CDP does not expose renderer PID directly. Same-site tabs share one renderer process -- not unique per tab. targetId is always 1:1 per tab.
SAME-TITLE DEDUP: multiple tabs with identical title -> MRU (LastActive) wins. TitleHistory prevents dynamic-title false misses ((3) Gmail and Gmail both resolve to same CdpTab).

WHY NOT HWND PROPS: SetProp interns the name into the global atom table (~16K practical limit) -- title-bearing keys with dynamic titles leak atoms unboundedly -> eventual system-wide failures (RegisterWindowMessage, clipboard). Also HWND is per-window not per-tab: all tabs share one HWND, and tab detach migrates renderer to a new HWND so props cannot follow. Identity lives in-process keyed by targetId only, rehydrated from Target.getTargets().

TAB MIGRATION: Detach-to-new-window and drag-into-another-window preserve the same targetId (renderer intact). Cache entry needs no migration -- only LastActive/Domain refresh on next Target.getTargets() poll. New title after migration is appended to TitleHistory (LRU cap=8), key unchanged.

IMPLEMENTATION STATUS: COMPLETE (2026-05-24).
Core change: WebCommands.Part1.cs PrintWebTarget() -- after CDP connect, calls cdp.GetTitleAsync() then appends tab:'<targetId[:8]>:<sanitizedTitle>' to grap before emitting OK.
Script updates: wkask.ps1 captures tab field; wkcdp.ps1 open handler parses tab; wkcdp-mon.ps1 shows targetId[:8] per tab line.
VERIFIED OUTPUT: OK {hwnd:0x00490200,proc:'chrome',cdp:9740,domain:'example.com',tab:'D27B3D0B:Example Domain'}
hwnd is non-zero when GA_ROOTOWNER (SDK launcher) resolves correct CASCADIA caller. tab is derived from CDP targetId (stable, session-unique), not HWND.
